title: Refactor Settings Routing and add resolution target policy
summary: Refactored the Settings Routing builder into an operator-first hierarchy, moved raw implementation controls into Advanced Routing Details, added persisted 1080p/1440p/4K height tolerance policy, and added Movie/TV target output-size fields for each height bucket.
reason: Operators could not tell which flat Routing fields were presets, direct media-policy controls, or advanced implementation details. The routing policy also treated middle-height sources as 4K for direct-copy bitrate and only exposed one Movie and one TV output-size target.
behavior_before: Settings Routing showed a flat implementation grid with ambiguous Processing Strategy, Enforcement Mode, Encode Target Mode, and Encoder Quality Preset controls. Direct-copy bitrate bucketing only had 1080-ish and 4K boundaries, and route size targets were single Movie/TV fallback values.
behavior_after: Settings Routing shows Library goal, What forces an encode, TV/Movie targets by 1080p/1440p/4K height, If encoded output is too large, and Video encoding. Python and PowerShell route decisions derive contiguous 1080p, 1440p, and 4K buckets from height tolerance percents; boundary values route to the higher bucket. Known-height sources use per-bucket Movie/TV output-size targets and bitrate caps, while unknown-height sources keep the legacy Movie/TV size and bitrate fallbacks.
